title: A finite-limit preserving functor transports scalar distributivity
statement: Let C,D be categories with Grothendieck topologies J,K, and let L : Sh(J,Set)→Sh(K,Set) preserve finite limits. Let X,Y be source sheaves, X',Y' target sheaves, and ex : X'≅L(X), ey : Y'≅L(Y). Let axV : X⊗X→X, ayV : Y⊗Y→Y, ax : X'⊗X'→X', ay : Y'⊗Y'→Y', and muV : X×Y→Y be arbitrary morphisms; tensor means sectionwise product. Let eV and eU be the canonical categorical-product-to-tensor isomorphisms. Set cx=eU(X',X')⁻¹ ≫ prod.map(ex,ex) ≫ (prodComparison L X X)⁻¹ ≫ L(eV(X,X)), and cy similarly using ey. Assume cx≫L(axV)≫ex⁻¹=ax and cy≫L(ayV)≫ey⁻¹=ay. Set nuV=eV(X,Y)⁻¹≫muV and nu=eU(X',Y')⁻¹≫prod.map(ex,ey)≫(prodComparison L X Y)⁻¹≫L(muV)≫ey⁻¹. If for every source section (r,s,x), nuV(axV(r,s),x)=ayV(nuV(r,x),nuV(s,x)), then for every target section (r,s,x), nu(ax(r,s),x)=ay(nu(r,x),nu(s,x)). All operations are arbitrary set-sheaf morphisms; no algebraic structures or adjunction hypotheses are imposed.

proof.text: By sectionwise extensionality, the hypothesis is the equality of the two distributivity morphisms from (X⊗X)⊗Y to Y.
Apply L. Naturality and invertibility of product comparisons transport projections, pairings, and the two addition maps. Conjugate by ex and ey and use the two addition compatibility equations.
Cancel comparison isomorphisms and evaluate the transported morphism equality at ((r,s),x).

lean.statement: theorem cartesianScalarDistributivityTransport {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D) (L : Sheaf J (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf K (Type u)) [PreservesFiniteLimits L] (X Y : Sheaf J (Type u)) (X' Y' : Sheaf K (Type u)) (ex : X' ≅ L.obj X) (ey : Y' ≅ L.obj Y) (axV : X ⊗ X ⟶ X) (ayV : Y ⊗ Y ⟶ Y) (ax : X' ⊗ X' ⟶ X') (ay : Y' ⊗ Y' ⟶ Y') (muV : X ⨯ Y ⟶ Y) : let eV := fun (P Q : Sheaf J (Type u)) ↦ (limit.isLimit (pair P Q)).conePointUniqueUpToIso (CartesianMonoidalCategory.tensorProductIsBinaryProduct P Q) let eU := fun (P Q : Sheaf K (Type u)) ↦ (limit.isLimit (pair P Q)).conePointUniqueUpToIso (CartesianMonoidalCategory.tensorProductIsBinaryProduct P Q) let cx := (eU X' X').inv ≫ prod.map ex.hom ex.hom ≫ inv (prodComparison L X X) ≫ L.map (eV X X).hom let cy := (eU Y' Y').inv ≫ prod.map ey.hom ey.hom ≫ inv (prodComparison L Y Y) ≫ L.map (eV Y Y).hom let nuV := (eV X Y).inv ≫ muV let nu := (eU X' Y').inv ≫ prod.map ex.hom ey.hom ≫ inv (prodComparison L X Y) ≫ L.map muV ≫ ey.inv cx ≫ L.map axV ≫ ex.inv = ax → cy ≫ L.map ayV ≫ ey.inv = ay → (∀ (W : Cᵒᵖ) (r s : X.obj.obj W) (x : Y.obj.obj W), nuV.hom.app W (axV.hom.app W (r, s), x) = ayV.hom.app W (nuV.hom.app W (r, x), nuV.hom.app W (s, x))) → ∀ (W : Dᵒᵖ) (r s : X'.obj.obj W) (x : Y'.obj.obj W), nu.hom.app W (ax.hom.app W (r, s), x) = ay.hom.app W (nu.hom.app W (r, x), nu.hom.app W (s, x))
